name: Jar wine
summary: Êđê jar wine from sticky rice and a leaf yeast, cloudy white, drunk by pulling straws from the same jar. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Bao Dak Lak on 30 Mar 2019 says Buon Ma Thuot Êđê wine has its own taste, even though the city is not the jar-wine capital.
howToEat: That account of a maker in Ako Dhong says the best wine is sticky rice, not the older corn or cassava jars. The yeast is galangal pounded with forest leaves. Rice is cooked on a wood fire, cooled, and mixed with yeast in a proportion that turns sour or bitter if it is off. After 7 to 10 days the rice goes into a jar that was washed and dried in hard sun. In that account the rice is packed twice, the second time three days later. Drinkable after more than three months, better at a year. Make it on a bright day.

The wine in that account is cloudy white, sweet, and fragrant. People pull the straws together. Bao Dak Lak on 23 May 2023 calls the same drink forest-leaf yeast and upland sticky rice. The Dak Lak provincial portal says Tết tables run from grilled meat to this jar, and does not name the animal. A cut for that meat, a strength, and a price are Check on arrival.
where: Ako Dhong is where Bao Dak Lak found the jars still being made. Drink it with the chicken and the bamboo rice at Ko Tam, or at Buon Tri A in Buon Don. Hours are Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Ruou can in Buon Ma Thuot — Ede jar wine in Ako Dhong
seoDescription: Ede jar wine from sticky rice and leaf yeast, cloudy white, shared from one jar. Ako Dhong still makes it. A strength and a price are Check on arrival.
taste: Bao Dak Lak on 30 Mar 2019 calls a finished jar cloudy white, sweet, fragrant, and refreshing, and says a long rest makes it deeper.
